texts: On day 300 of Year 1, the keepers of the Harbor Row lit the lanterns of the Harbor Row at sundown.
A crowd of nightmoths gathered at the Harbor Row.
Three sky-cats descended from the cliff-spires.
The three sky-cats hunted the nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row.
The nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row shrank.
Each nightmoth that survived the hunt fled to the Hollows.
The lanterns at the Hollows gained silken threads that night.
The three sky-cats molted during the hunt.
Feathers fell to the base of the cliff.
Nightmoths left silken threads on the lanterns of the Harbor Row.
The keepers of the Harbor Row collected the silken threads from the lanterns at dawn on day 301 of Year 1.

q1_issues.issue: The per-member distribution rule asserts that each keeper lit the entire lantern group, a stronger claim than the sentence's cumulative reading, and the same whole-group-object copying recurs in the rules at indices 26, 74, 96 and 105.
"The three sky-cats molted" gives the intransitive subject Agent, but molting is an internal change of state the subject undergoes, which the intransitive-subject test assigns Patient.
"left silken threads on the lanterns" makes the threads Patient, but depositing them neither creates, destroys, consumes nor physically changes them, so the object-change test gives Theme.

q2_gaps: A cumulative reading over two grouped plurals in one clause ("the keepers lit the lanterns", "nightmoths left silken threads on the lanterns"): the only licensed distribution shape hands each member the whole group-level predication, so "each did some" is inexpressible.

A day-of-year ordinal date ("on day 300 of Year 1", "at dawn on day 301 of Year 1"): the calendar term set pairs (Day n) with (Month ...) as a day-of-month, so a bare day-of-year ordinal is stored indistinguishably from a day-of-month.
review.notes: Coreference and witness indexing, the "that night" term propagation, the Hollows Name-only plural label, and the each-plus-relative-clause rule are all handled correctly. "of the Harbor Row" as an opaque Possession is defensible, though it could also read as an agent-nominalization argument.

issues.reason: `(Implication (PartOf $x sk_keeper_1) (… (Patient (sk_light $x) sk_lantern_1) …))` at strength 1.0 asserts that every keeper lit the whole lantern group, which is more than "the keepers lit the lanterns" states (*Core patterns*: never assert more than the text states), and the same whole-group object is copied into the rules at indices 26, 74, 96 and 105.

`Agent` is defined as the volitional doer and *Thematic roles* says an intransitive subject that undergoes the eventuality is never `Agent` by default — molting is an internal, non-volitional change of state of the cats, so the intransitive test gives `Patient`.

`Patient` is reserved for an object the action creates, destroys, consumes or physically changes; leaving threads on a lantern only deposits them unchanged, so the stated test (and its "when unclear, default to `Theme`" fallback) gives `Theme`.

gaps_confirmed: a cumulative reading over two grouped plurals in one clause ("the keepers lit the lanterns", "nightmoths left silken threads on the lanterns", "the lanterns produced mist-light"): the only licensed distribution shape hands each member the whole group-level predication, so "each member did some of it" has no form

a day-of-year ordinal date ("day 300 / day 301 of Year 1"): `(Day <n>)` is defined as a day-of-month paired with `(Month …)`, so a bare day-of-year ordinal is stored indistinguishably from a day-of-month
new_gaps: an AGENT noun taking an of-phrase ("the keepers of the Harbor Row") satisfies both the nominalization-object test of *Complements of nouns and adjectives* ("keeper of X" ≈ "one who keeps X" → `(Of …)`) and the relational/role carve-out that keeps the genitive `Possession`; the instruction set does not say which wins, so two faithful parses can differ
adjudication.defect_summary: Issue 0: the compliant form is the group-level event alone — `(Member sk_light_1 light) (Agent sk_light_1 sk_keeper_1) (Patient sk_light_1 sk_lantern_1)` plus its time/tense atoms with NO per-member rule, since group-as-unit predication is the default of *Coordination & plurals* and a distribution rule over a whole-group object over-asserts (the same deletion applies to the rules at indices 26, 74, 96, 105), while the cumulative "each keeper lit some of the lanterns" has no licensed form at all. Issue 1: `(Patient sk_molt_1 sk_group_1)`, and the same swap inside the e11 rule. Issue 2: `(Theme sk_leave_1 sk_thread_2)`, and the same swap inside the e13 rule.
adjudication.notes: The rest of the passage is handled well: coreference and witness indexing across three groups of lanterns/threads/nightmoths, the `Hollows` Name-only plural label, "that night" term propagation, the each+relative-clause rule with its `QuantifierPhrase` companion, and the correct omission of an entity-level position atom for "left threads on the lanterns" (event `Location` only, per the granary rule).
